description: A ref:// link in a message opens the code it points at, snapshotted when the message was sent.
agent_instructions: Switchboard renders ref:// links as a code viewer. Write a markdown link whose destination is ref://path/to/file.ts, optionally followed by :Scope:Name waypoints and an optional #matcher; the file is snapshotted at send time and attached automatically, so the reader sees the code as it was when you wrote about it. Waypoints match any descendant, so ref://app.tsx:App:handleSubmit works through unnamed layers, and A::B::method is accepted for C++. Use :arguments for a parameter list, and :arguments:name for one parameter. Matchers: #text highlights the first match inside the resolved scope; #text@before:anchor and #text@after:anchor pick the occurrence nearest before or after another string; #from..to spans a range. Encoding: percent-encode a space as %20 (a raw space ends the link destination and the ref degrades to plain text), and percent-encode a literal .. or @ inside matched code so it is not read as a range or an anchor. A ref inside a code fence or inline code is never detected, so documenting this format costs nothing. A malformed ref fails the send with the position, so fix it and resend. Refs only work in channel_reply and notify_human; a crosstalk_send body is not scanned, so a ref written there arrives as an unopenable link.
